487: pub fn trim_ascii_prefix(

489:     slice: &[u8],
490:     range: Match,
491: ) -> Match {
492:     fn is_space(b: u8) -> bool {
493:         match b {
494:             b'\t' | b'\n' | b'\x0B' | b'\x0C' | b'\r' | b' ' => true,
495:             _ => false,
496:         }
497:     }

499:     let count = slice[range]

502:             is_space(b) && !line_term.as_bytes().contains(&b)
503:         })

508: pub fn find_iter_at_in_context<M, F>(
509:     searcher: &Searcher,
510:     matcher: M,
511:     mut bytes: &[u8],
512:     range: std::ops::Range<usize>,
513:     mut matched: F,
514: ) -> io::Result<()>
515: where
516:     M: Matcher,
517:     F: FnMut(Match) -> bool,
518: {
519:     // This strange dance is to account for the possibility of look-ahead in
520:     // the regex. The problem here is that mat.bytes() doesn't include the
521:     // lines beyond the match boundaries in mulit-line mode, which means that
522:     // when we try to rediscover the full set of matches here, the regex may no
523:     // longer match if it required some look-ahead beyond the matching lines.
524:     //
525:     // PCRE2 (and the grep-matcher interfaces) has no way of specifying an end
526:     // bound of the search. So we kludge it and let the regex engine search the
527:     // rest of the buffer... But to avoid things getting too crazy, we cap the
528:     // buffer.
529:     //
530:     // If it weren't for multi-line mode, then none of this would be needed.
531:     // Alternatively, if we refactored the grep interfaces to pass along the
532:     // full set of matches (if available) from the searcher, then that might
533:     // also help here. But that winds up paying an upfront unavoidable cost for
534:     // the case where matches don't need to be counted. So then you'd have to
535:     // introduce a way to pass along matches conditionally, only when needed.
536:     // Yikes.
537:     //
